purpose: The matrix uses 28 references twice, on 56 rows. Every pair is two different texts. This file is the canonical key for traceability: a package reference resolves to exactly one xlsx row. Without it, a traceability entry citing "22.3.1" names two different capabilities.
convention: The first occurrence keeps the bare reference. The second takes a "b" suffix, following CF-33a. A carve-out preserved from a retired text takes an "a" suffix on a new number.

5.5.rule: B supersedes A. B is a strict superset in all four pairs. Two details in A are not carried by B and are preserved as new package references.

5.6.rule: NOT a supersession. The pairing by number is coincidental — only 5.6.1 matches concept to concept. Both blocks are retained in full; B takes a suffixed package reference.

8.1.rule: Two unrelated capabilities sharing one number. **A is finance, B is AI governance.** A (rows 1728–1733) is no-show deferred-to-earned revenue recognition, no-show reporting, complimentary and invitation PLUs, who issued an invitation, and issuance restricted by profile — **none of which is AI or reporting, and all of which belongs in `finance`**. B (rows 1734–1739) is prompt logging, response logging, approval before execution, explainability with confidence indicators, and an AI audit trail. **B stays in the AI domain and is nearly contracted already**: `ai.interaction` records prompt and response under ADR-0020, and `x-ticvai-permission-escalated` is the approval gate 8.1.4 asks for. **A keeps the bare reference; B takes the `b` suffix**, following CF-33a. Decided by Chinmay 18 August — the split is ours to make and only the numbering needed sign-off.
8.1.bDomain: ai — governance, largely met by ADR-0020

22.3.rule: Two unrelated capabilities sharing one number. **A is case management, B is journey automation.** A (rows 2901–2910) is case creation, classification, assignment, workflow, SLA, escalation, agent notes, omnichannel tracking, reporting and audit trail — **the contract CF-99 built**. B (rows 2911–2920) is a visual journey builder, event trigger engine, multi-channel automation, conditional logic, wait controls, abandoned cart recovery, membership and loyalty lifecycle automation, wallet automation and birthday campaigns — **CF-137's journey automation**. **This is the dangerous pair**: `22.3.6` named both *Case Escalation Management* and *Abandoned Cart Recovery*, so CF-99 built against A while CF-83 had counsel reviewing B under one number. **A keeps the bare reference; B takes the `b` suffix.** Decided by Chinmay 18 August.

a.text: The system should support a ticketing data model which allows a guest to purchase and manage multiple tickets (portfolio of tickets) under their account.

b.text: Support purchase, ownership, management, and consumption of multiple tickets, passes, memberships, and entitlements under a single portfolio.

a.text: The system should allow multiple portfolios to be linked only to one account.

b.text: Support multiple portfolios linked to a single account representing individuals, dependents, employees, students, or group participants.

a.text: The system should provide the ability to move stored credit between portfolios linked to different accounts. For Example: each family member have their own portfolio with the possibility to transfer part of the stored credit between the portfolios enabled in the system. At the end, each expenditure should be tracked independently by portfolio (family member).

b.text: Allow configurable transfer of stored value, wallet balances, promotional credits, and vouchers between linked portfolios with full audit tracking.

a.text: The system should be able to print media which are linked to guest's portfolios, this way multiple media can be availed/printed to the same guest portfolio. (examples: lost/soiled ticket reprints, website order's printing  QR code prints)

b.text: Support issuance and management of QR codes, RFID wristbands, RFID cards, NFC passes, digital tickets, and printed tickets linked to portfolios.

a.text: VIP / Priority Handling: Separate or fast-track queues for premium guests.

b.text: Automatically assign guests to queues based on ticket type, attraction, capacity availability, reservation rules, guest profile, or business policies.

a.text: Load Balancing: Redirect customers to less busy queues/rides/entry points.

b.text: Configure queue capacities by hour, day, attraction, session, ticket type, membership level, or sales channel.

a.text: SMS, email, or whats app , app push notifications when it’s nearly their turn.

b.text: Allow authorized users to add, remove, move, prioritize, or reassign guests within queues.

a.text: Real-time updates on remaining wait time.

b.text: Support priority queueing for VIP guests, annual pass holders, premium packages, loyalty tiers, and accessibility requirements.

a.text: Accessibility Features: Special accommodations for disabled or elderly guests based on the profile of the customer

b.text: Automatically recommend or redirect guests to alternative attractions or queues.

carve_outs.text: Expenditure shall be tracked independently by portfolio. A family transferring stored credit between member portfolios must still see each member's spend attributed to that member.
carve_outs.why: 5.5.3A states per-portfolio expenditure attribution. 5.5.3B states transfer with audit tracking, which is not the same thing — an audit trail of transfers does not attribute downstream spend.

carve_outs.text: Media linked to a portfolio shall be reissuable — lost or soiled ticket reprints, and printing of media for orders placed on the web.
carve_outs.why: 5.5.4B enumerates media types. It does not state the reissue case, which is an operation with its own authorisation and audit requirements.
